title: Wet-lab identification of Leishmania donovani antigens detected by human IgG1
author: Bruno Hinckel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.u8rezv6
materials: Prepare 10x solutions of cathode buffer (Tris 1M, Tricine 1M, SDS 1%, pH ~8,25) and anode buffer (Tris 1M, HCl 0.225M, pH 8.9)
Cover the transfer system with the lid
Add the polymerising agents: 67.5 µl of 10% APS solutions and 6.75 µl of TEMED
Soak three layers of blotting paper (Whatman GB005) with blotting buffer (300 mM Tris, 100 mM acetic acid (pH 8.6). Do not flood the semi-dry system (1703940, Bio-Rad, UK)
To reveal the protein bands, dissolve 1 tablet pair of SigmaFast DAB (D0426, Sigma-Aldrich) in 15ml of dH 2 O immediately prior to use.

steps.title: Prepare Stock Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary stock solutions for gel casting.

substeps.instruction: Prepare AB-3 stock solution by dissolving 48 g of acrylamide and 1.5 g of bisacrylamide (twice-crystallized; Serva) in 100 ml of water.
Prepare 3x gel buffer solution (Tris 3M, HCl 1M, SDS 0.3%, pH 8.45).

steps.title: Cast Resolving Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and pour the 10% resolving gel.

substeps.instruction: Mix 4 ml of AB-3, 6.66 ml of 3x gel buffer solution, and 9.33 ml of dH2O to prepare 20 ml of 10% resolving gel solution.
Add 100 µl of 10% ammonium persulphate (APS) and 10 µl of TEMED to the solution.
Pour the solution into the gel apparatus using a pipette, leaving a space approximately the height of the comb plus 1.5 cm for the stacking gel.
Store the gel overnight at 4°C with a dH2O overlay and cover with plastic film to minimize evaporation.

steps.title: Cast Stacking Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and pour the 4% stacking gel on the following day.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pour off the dH2O from the top of the solidified resolving gel.
Prepare 4 ml of 4% stacking gel solution by mixing 0.33 ml of AB-3, 1 ml of 3x gel buffer, and 2.67 ml of dH2O.
Pour the 4% stacking gel solution onto the top of the resolving gel using a pipette.
Directly insert the comb, avoiding the formation of air bubbles underneath.
Store the gel at 4°C until the stacking gel is completely solidified.

steps.title: Prepare Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare L. donovani lysate samples for loading.

substeps.instruction: Mix 3 parts L. donovani lysate with 1 part non-reducing sample buffer (2% SDS (wt/vol), 30% glycerol (wt/vol), 0.05% Coomassie blue G-250 (Serva), 150 mM Tris/HCl (pH 7.0)).
Dilute with PBS if necessary to achieve a final total protein load of 4 µg/mm lane.
Mount the electrophoresis apparatus and fill cathode and anode tanks with 1x cathode and anode buffer, respectively.
Carefully and slowly remove the comb to avoid damaging the stacking gel.
Rinse the wells multiple times with dH2O.
Load the wells with prepared samples and protein molecular weight marker (1610374, Bio-Rad, UK).
Run the gel at 30V constant for 55 min, then at 120V constant for a total of 5 h.

steps.title: Transfer Proteins to Membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer separated proteins from the gel to a nitrocellulose (NC) membrane.

substeps.instruction: Place the NC membrane (10600046, GE Healthcare Life Sciences, UK) on top of soaked blotting paper.
Carefully place the gel on top of the NC membrane, ensuring full contact across the whole surface.
Add four layers of blotting paper soaked in blotting buffer on top of the gel, adding more buffer if necessary without flooding.
Squeeze out air bubbles by gently rolling a cylindrical object (e.g., a Falcon tube) against the top layer of blotting paper.
Run the transfer for 120 minutes at constant 60 mA.
Air dry the membranes upon completion, placing heavy objects on the four corners to avoid curling.

steps.title: Block and Slice Membrane
steps.instruction: Block the membrane to prevent non-specific binding and cut into strips.

substeps.instruction: Block the membrane with blocking buffer (PBS + 3% w/v non-fat milk powder) overnight at 4°C.
Wash three times for 5 minutes each in PBST (PBS + 0.05% Tween 20), followed by one wash of PBST + 0.02% w/v sodium azide.
Tape the top of the membrane for identification.
Slice the blocked NC membrane into 4 mm strips using a paper trimmer (Cathedral Products, UK).

steps.title: Primary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate membrane strips with serum samples.

substeps.instruction: Pre-wet individual strips with PBS and place them in wells of an 8-well immunotray (octa-101, Pateof, Denmark).
Number the strips sequentially (including the MWM).
Add serum samples diluted 1:400 in blocking buffer to cover the strips.
Incubate at rocking for 1 h at room temperature (RT).
Wash the strips with PBST six times for 10 minutes each.

steps.title: Secondary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate strips with HRP-conjugated secondary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Add mouse anti-human IgG1-HRP (ab99774, Abcam, UK) diluted 1:1000 in blocking buffer to cover the strips.
Incubate at rocking for 1 h at RT.
Wash the strips with PBST six times for 10 minutes each.

steps.title: Detection and Storage
steps.instruction: Develop the signal and store the strips.

substeps.instruction: Wash the strips thoroughly with water.
Add enough volume to cover the strips and incubate for 4 minutes in darkness.
Air-dry the strips with heavy objects on top and bottom to avoid curling.
Store strips in airtight containers at 4°C until use.
